title: Audio Editing Tricks
intro: Comping, crossfades, timing and pitch — where a good take becomes a great one.

tips.t: Put take-switching on keys you choose
tips.d: Press ⌥K to open the Key Commands window and type “Take” in the search field. Find Select Previous Take or Comp and Select Next Take or Comp, which step through the takes and comps listed in the take folder’s pop-up menu. Check what they are assigned to, and put them on keys you can reach while you audition.

src.label: Apple — Assign key commands in Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Create custom keyboard shortcuts for Logic Pro for Mac
Apple — Preview take recordings in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Save your comp as a new comp before changing it
tips.d: The take folder menu has “Duplicate Comp”. Do this before every significant change and you can always go back to the version that was working.

src.label: Apple — Create and save comps in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Move a comp edit point without redoing the comp
tips.d: Drag the vertical divider between two take sections to slide the edit point earlier or later.

src.label: Apple — Edit comps in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Curve the fade after you draw it
tips.d: With the Fade tool, hover over the middle of a fade you've made and drag left or right to change its curve. Or select the region and adjust the fade's Curve value in the Region inspector.

src.label: Why Logic Pro Rules - How to Get the Most Out of Logic Pro X's Fade Tool
Apple — Edit fades in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

tips.t: Use “Remove Silence from Audio Region” on a live kit or spoken word
tips.d: Select the audio region and press ⌃X (Remove Silence from Audio Region). Everything below a threshold you set is removed, and new regions are created from what remains. That makes it useful for a live kit or spoken word.

src.label: studio-interns.com — Remove Silence from Audio Region… ⌃X
9to5Mac — Editing noisy audio files with Remove Silence in Logic Pro X
Apple — Uses for Remove Silence in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Add a tiny fade to the start of every region as policy
tips.d: Even 3 ms removes the click from a non‑zero‑crossing start. Do it to everything and you never chase a mystery click again.

tips.t: Add flex markers either side before you move one
tips.d: Placing anchor markers on the neighbouring transients stops your edit from stretching the whole bar.

src.label: Apple — Flex tool time stretching in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.d: Give the audio track a Flex mode and make sure Flex is selected for the region in the Region inspector. You can then quantize that audio by choosing a value from the Quantize pop-up menu in the Region inspector. It's real-time, so you can change the value later, or turn it off to get the original timing back.

src.label: macProVideo - Quantizing In Logic: The Essentials
Sound On Sound - Logic Pro: Editing Drum Timings
Apple — Quantize regions in Logic Pro (Logic Pro 10.7 guide)

tips.t: Use Flex Pitch to fix a single flat note
tips.d: Switch the track's Flex mode to Flex Pitch, then drag the note blob vertically. The gain, vibrato, pitch drift and formant handles are all on the same blob.

src.label: Apple — Edit pitch and timing with Flex Pitch in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Reset all Flex edits rather than undoing repeatedly
tips.d: Control-click the flexed region and choose Reset All Flex Edits. It clears the region's flex data and starts you fresh.

src.label: Apple — Delete, reset and move flex markers in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Use the Audio File Editor for true destructive edits
tips.d: Double‑click a region and switch to the File tab. Silence, reverse, normalise and pencil‑edit at the sample level. Changes here affect the file itself.

src.label: Apple — Audio File Editor overview in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Change region level non‑destructively with Gain
tips.d: The Region inspector's Gain parameter changes playback level without touching the file. Always try this before normalising.

src.label: Apple — Change gain of audio regions in the Tracks area (Logic Pro for Mac)

tips.t: Reclaim disk space with Project Management > Clean Up
tips.d: Once your comps are final, choose File > Project Management > Clean Up. Its options are Delete Unused Audio Files, Delete Unreferenced Audio Files and Delete Backups, and files are deleted from disk. A dialog lists everything to be deleted, so deselect the Delete checkbox for anything you want to keep, and back up first.

src.label: Apple — Clean up Logic Pro for Mac projects
Apple — Remove unused audio files in your Logic Pro for Mac project

tips.t: Reverse a region, destructively or not
tips.d: Select the region, then Functions > Reverse in the Audio File Editor, or apply the Reverse setting in the region inspector for a non‑destructive version.

src.label: Apple — Reverse audio regions in Logic Pro for Mac

tips.t: Commit edits with Bounce Regions in Place
tips.d: When you are happy with a comp, select the regions and choose File > Bounce > Regions in Place. In the dialog, set the name and a Destination: New Track, or Selected Track to replace the regions. Set Source to Leave, Mute or Delete, and decide whether to Bypass Effect Plug-ins. Choose Leave or Mute to keep the original.

src.label: Apple — Bounce regions in place in Logic Pro for Mac
